quotes.text: Endix makes the demo experience feel like it should have always been this simple.
The potential, with this level of execution, is insane.
Endix may offer one of the more unique experiences of the showcase season.
One of the most ambitious and accessible virtual gaming showcases on the internet.
It feels like someone mashed up a traditional expo with a multiplayer hub world, and the result is surprisingly immersive.
More importantly, it shows what a gaming expo can be.
A virtual gaming expo with huge PlayStation Home energy.
Each iteration of Endix feels bigger, more polished, and more confident.
ENDIX is so good, and honestly, I want to see it grow and frankly, grow with it.
Endix Is Turning Digital Game Showcases Into a Playable Experience.
The strongest part of ENDIX is the event’s accessibility.
It is easy, fast, and surprisingly social.
No expensive tickets. No travel. No hotel bookings.
ENDIX absolutely has its own charm.
The event feels like it is growing in the right direction.
ENDIX presents an opportunity for developers and players to interact through digital worlds, and I’m here for it.
It’s well worth your time – ENDIX stands out from its peers as a wholly unique indie gaming event and I can’t wait to go back.

Most importantly, ENDIX still offers something rare in the games industry: a genuinely accessible virtual convention space that tries to bring players, creators, press, developers, and publishers together without putting financial barriers in front of people.
However, PS Home vibes aside, ENDIX absolutely has its own charm and, rough edges aside, it’s a fun way to explore upcoming titles.

Whether that approach becomes a larger part of the industry’s future depends on the adoption, but for players looking for something more interactive than another livestream, Endix may offer one of the more unique experiences of the showcase season.

What makes ENDIX so unique is that the team behind it has worked hard to create a virtual world for ENDIX that allows players to walk around its video game world in order to see what the future of the gaming industry has in store for them.
Because of this, ENDIX occasionally genuinely feels like walking through a digital convention together with other attendees, something many other online events still completely lack.
Endix leans into the idea that if we are going to do a digital event, it should feel like a place worth exploring, not just a menu of trailers.
As such, events like ENDIX are amazing to me in the sense that they make both attendance and showcasing very accessible.

IGN will also be hosting all of the biggest trailers from ENDIX on IGN.com and our IGN and GameTrailers YouTube channels, so you'll be able to check out this great selection of titles whenever you'd like.

reviews.text: This is a very nice concept of finding about games and promotions! Easily and freely accessible for everyone! Great aeshetics with nice touch of each of the participants. The giveaways are a nice bonus as well and mini-games are addicting!

An amazing experience/showcase. A place where you can see trailers for upcoming indie games, with fun experiences built in for each game by the devs. Really well though out and executed. Most of the negative reviews you see are from salty people who only got in for free keys, therefore before you decide, hop in and see for yourself. There's nothing like it.
It's fun to explore and does exactly what it's supposed to do, show you upcoming games. Beware the maze.
A cool experience within the virtual platforms, definitely worth going to if you can.
